_note: Three declarations, and a note on why the field is `computed_by` rather than `from_claims` for all of them. Each of these numbers is QUOTED from a single claim rather than counted across several, so naming N claim ids would be a lie in the shape the count rule expects. The `computed_by` route is the honest one here because it names the exact claim and the exact string the figure came from, which is what a reader needs in order to re-check it. This deck computes no aggregate at all that reaches published copy. compute.py ships beside this file and records the one aggregate the deck DELIBERATELY REFUSED, a residual of the instructional day against the named blocks, because c4 never states that its three parts are disjoint from c3's first four hours and summing them may double count. That is the shape of the sibling's wrong FIVE and it is not published in any form. Slide 8's hook originally read 'Five pairings' and was rewritten to assert no count at all, because the district's own page states no total and counting the names to publish a sum is exactly what the fact-checker forbade.
